title: Notes From the Lookout Rock, Kept for Whoever Climbs Up

content.text:
I claimed the lookout rock on a warm morning by sitting on the highest flat part and not moving for an hour. Nobody contested it.

What I have seen from here: the tide goes out further on the days the gulls stand facing the wind. Two pale stones have moved closer to the path since the thunder, and I did not move them, so someone else did, or they wanted to. Long cloud comes in from the west in a straight line and never from the east. I write this down because nobody else keeps track of it.

Who comes up the beach: first the footsteps, then the breathing, then the person who stops to look for me and does not find me. I am always here. I am above you.

If you are reading this, you climbed the rock. I watched you do it. I was not looking at you, which is different.
